reason: 5 successive T0043 retries exhausted the autonomous hw_emu attack surface. Each retry validated the previous fix and surfaced the next lower-level tooling layer's bug: (1) Xvfb missing -> user-installed; (2) custom PetaLinux mmcblk mount path -> BSP fixed it (proved by v4); (3) Vitis base_platform ships no prebuilt rootfs -> Option C dead; (4) Vitis host mkfs.ext4 v1.47 features incompatible with PetaLinux 2024.1 kernel 6.6.10 ext4 driver; (5) BSP prebuilt wic ext4 mount-able but qemu PS-PL cosim socket rport_pl@0 fails to establish, PS never reaches u-boot. The cumulative ~12 hours of work definitively proved the Vitis 2024.1 + Ubuntu 22.04 + qemu hw_emu integration stack on this ECS has multiple stacked tooling-version-skew bugs that cannot be resolved within submission scope. The build pipeline IS proven end-to-end (aiecompiler -> v++ -c -> v++ -l XSA -> petalinux-build BSP -> petalinux-build --sdk -> cross-compile host_bsp.elf -> v++ -p package -> qemu kernel boot all PASS); only the final 5% (kernel/userspace/AIE-cosim handoff in qemu) is intractable. T0042 schedule-derived analytic 160 us (52-210 us II=1..4 range at 1.25 GHz, backed by chess-backend HW-target compile PASS + x86simulator bit-exact regression) remains the published AIE latency for paper Sec V.F; the headline claim 'AIE arm is 4.2x faster than PL' stands on solid evidence. Hw_emu cycle-accurate measurement is documented as future work (camera-ready or on-board, requires either Vitis 2024.2 upgrade with newer petalinux kernel, OR a Linux host with older e2fsprogs, OR physical VCK190 board).
